references.text: Beersheba is first mentioned here when Abraham made a covenant with Abimelech and named the place Beersheba.
Isaac also named a well Sheba, and the city was called Beersheba after this.
Beersheba is also mentioned as part of Simeon's inheritance, which was taken from Judah's territory.
In 1 Chronicles, Beersheba is listed as one of the cities where Simeon's descendants lived.
After the exile, Judah's descendants settled again in Beersheba and the surrounding areas.
